speaker: Sheldon
text: You. A menial job. Like yours.

speaker: Unknown_speaker044
text: So, Mr. Cooper, you're looking for a job. Why, thank you for noticing. I'm menial employee of the month. Do you have a particular field in mind?

speaker: Sheldon
text: I do. For thousands of years, the lowest classes of the human race have spent their lives laboring to erect monuments under the lash of their betters, until finally they dropped down and became one with the dust through which they trudged.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Do you have anything like that?

speaker: Unknown_speaker044
text: I didn't really have to. So how about construction?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Oh, that would be good. Sawing, hammering, eating out of a lunch pail as my working class fellows and I sit perched precariously on a girder high above the metropolis.

speaker: Unknown_speaker044
text: No, no, this is putting up sheetrock at a housing project in Rosemead.

speaker: Sheldon
text: I could do that. One question. What's sheetrock?

speaker: Unknown_speaker044
text: Moving on. How about doing deliveries for a florist? Do you have your own car?

speaker: Sheldon
text: That seems acceptable. I don't drive.

speaker: Unknown_speaker044
text: Of course you don't. Mr. Cooper, let me just ask you a question. What was your last job?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Senior theoretical particle physicist at Caltech focusing on M theory, or in layman's terms, string theory.

speaker: Unknown_speaker044
